source.title: OledFL: Unleashing the Potential of Decentralized Federated Learning via Opposite Lookahead Enhancement
source.authors: Qing-Lun Li; Miao Zhang; Mengzhu Wang; Quan-Jun Yin; Li Shen

record.file_problem: Supplied full paper text; some figures are garbled, but the relevant numerical results are also reported in tables and prose.
record.tranche_reason: Extends generalization experiments and stability analysis to decentralized federated learning on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 under IID and heterogeneous client data; it does not test the catalog's ordinary centralized memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, or sharpness versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper measures test accuracy and theoretical stability/generalization bounds for federated training. These outcomes bear on the claim's broad generalization subject, but its experiments compare federated algorithms and data partitions rather than testing V1–V8 as specified. Reported gains from OledFL are rows for federated test accuracy under V1 as a broad natural-label generalization outcome; they do not establish random-label memorization or any of V2–V8. The paper also discusses flatter loss landscapes, but reports no magnitude-aware perturbation measure. Theoretical bounds and cited findings are not experimental outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its own federated optimization method and uses the flat-minima explanation to interpret its performance. It tests none of V1–V8: natural-label test accuracy alone does not test V1's coexistence with random-label memorization, and qualitative loss landscapes do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that OledFL improves convergence speed and test performance, narrows the decentralized–centralized federated performance gap, and can surpass the tested centralized methods. They also derive convergence and uniform-stability generalization bounds under stated assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: Opposite-lookahead initialization is added to decentralized federated optimizers; experiments use federated CIFAR training rather than the original versions' specified interventions and settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported test performance varies with dataset, IID versus Dirichlet or Pathological client partition, communication topology, client count, local epochs, Ole parameter β, and SAM perturbation radius λ.

fits_no_version.finding: OledFL-SGD and OledFL-SAM improve test accuracy over their corresponding decentralized baselines in the recorded CIFAR-10/100 partitions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Opposite-lookahead initialization improves decentralized federated image-classification accuracy in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 4–5 qualitatively depict a flatter, lower-loss landscape for OledFL-SAM than DFedSAM on CIFAR-10 Dir 0.3. No magnitude-aware sharpness statistic or empirical generalization-gap ranking is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this federated comparison, opposite-lookahead initialization yields visually flatter loss landscapes alongside higher test accuracy.

record.problems: The experiments report test accuracy, not paired training and test error or random-label memorization. Architecture and parameter counts are not stated in the supplied text. Figure-based sweeps are not extracted where exact values are not reported in prose or tables.
record.rows_left_out: No additional tabulated test-accuracy rows retained beyond the CIFAR-10/100 Dir 0.3 and IID conditions shown above; the numerous Dirichlet, Pathological, and topology-specific table entries are omitted to prioritize representative natural-label test outcomes. Figure-only curves and hyperparameter sweeps are not entered as precise-value rows.

untested.parts: Coexistence of fitting fixed random labels and generalizing on natural labels with the same architecture and recipe; random-label held-out accuracy.
Test-error changes with width beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty. Local epochs and client counts are different interventions.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, underfitting, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus measured train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded values and baselines match Table II. The rows belong under the separate federated-method finding, not V1. Uniform-stability bounds and qualitative flatness comparisons supply no additional test of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label accuracy; no small Inception, AlexNet, or MLP memorization comparison. Natural-label CIFAR test accuracy is evaluated in a decentralized federated setting.
